subject: Tail-latency pileup impacting MediaSet — batching & queue-depth mitigation requested
messages:
From: Sophie Park <sophie@mediaset.io>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-29T23:05:00Z
Subject: Spike in tail latency (p95/p99) since 23:00 UTC — MediaSet production

Hi Vanessa,

Since ~23:00 UTC last night we've been seeing our p95 jump from ~180ms to ~1.2s and p99 to ~3.4s on the Hosted API calls that hit the 'text-generation' endpoint. Error rate has stayed low but throughput is steady (~120 requests/s). This coincides with a large batch of very small prompts (avg seq_len ~45 tokens) from our mobile chat clients. The issue is causing visible UI hitches for end users and a spike in support tickets.

We've attached a short sample of request IDs and timestamps. Severity: SEV2 for us. Can you provide an ETA for a mitigation and a recommended temporary workaround (e.g., route to Dedicated or lower-latency model variant)? We can put traffic into a fallback if you recommend it.

Thanks,
Sophie Park
Customer Success Lead, MediaSet
Attachment: mediaset-latency-sample-logs.txt (text)
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Sophie Park <sophie@mediaset.io>
Date: 2028-04-30T00:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Spike in tail latency (p95/p99) since 23:00 UTC — MediaSet production

Sophie — thanks for the quick signal and the samples. Looping in engineering and SRE to triage immediately: Marcus, Stephanie, Rishi, Laura — please join a bridge in 15 minutes. Initial asks for triage: check batch window growth, queue depth per serving shard, autoscaler activity, and KV cache miss rate for MediaSet's routing key.

Customer impact is visible in production UIs; Sophie asked for an ETA and a workaround. I want a short mitigation plan we can push in the next 20 minutes (config change + routing fallback). Also please prepare wording for an update I can send to MediaSet CSMs.

I'll host the bridge at zoom.me/1234 in 10min.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, NA
Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-30T00:10:30Z
Subject: Re: Spike in tail latency (initial findings)

On 2028-04-30 00:02, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com wrote:
> Sophie — thanks for the quick signal ...

Short SRE runbook output / findings (10m sliding window):
- Batch window latency: median batching delay rose from ~12ms -> ~95ms on GPU pool g1. Continuous batching logic increased window to aggregate throughput for many small prompts, which inflated p95.
- Queue depth: per-serving-shard pending queue rose from ~8 -> ~76 requests on 3/12 hosts, causing head-of-line blocking and elevated tail latency.
- Autoscaler: did not add new workers because the autoscaler uses a sustained-concurrency trigger; the observed traffic is highly bursty and confused the policy.
- KV cache: a spike in KV cache misses for model variant 'redwood-alpha-1' due to mixed prompt prefixes from MediaSet routing keys, increasing per-request token work.

Immediate mitigations I'm pushing now (ETA: 2-6 minutes to take effect):
1) Set route-specific max_batch_time_ms=30 and max_batch_size=16 for MediaSet to limit batch window expansion.
2) Enforce a per-customer concurrency cap of 30 to bound queue depth (temporary, 30m).
3) Flip 100% of MediaSet traffic to 'redwood-alpha-1-q4-lowlat' (quantized low-latency variant) for 12m while we observe tail behavior.
4) Warm small-sequence compiled kernels and pre-populate KV caches on affected hosts.
5) If tail persists after 12m, fallback option: route high-priority customer requests to a reserved Dedicated pool (requires exec approval for credits).

Attaching the quick mitigation runbook and the sample log we received. I'll post a short status update after the config push.

-marcus
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: mitigation_runbook.pdf (pdf)
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: marcusslin? But internal names only are allowed so: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-30T00:18:00Z
Subject: Escalation to Exec: approval for temporary credits & Dedicated fallback for MediaSet

Team — quick exec ask to approve an emergency path: if the low-latency variant and batch caps don't fully restore p95/p99 within 12 minutes, we should offer MediaSet a temporary migration to a small Dedicated pool for their high-priority route while we complete a deeper fix. Estimated cost exposure: up to $50k for a 24-hour Dedicated lease and handoff support.

Ask:
- Rishi / Laura: greenlight up to $50k emergency credits and priority infra staffing to create & attach a Dedicated pool for MediaSet.
- Stephanie: prepare customer-facing language and an offer (credits + 24/7 on-call during the migration).
- Marcus: continue mitigation steps and confirm rollback criteria.

MediaSet impact: user-visible latency spikes (p95 ~1.2s, p99 ~3.4s). They're a high-touch account (Enterprise) and a small outage window has downstream revenue risk. I want to be able to offer a clean fallback so the CSM can reduce churn risk.

I'll send to Sophie with the approved credits language once I have a thumbs up.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, NA
Redwood Inference
